title: Southern Nevada Amendments to the 2023 National Electrical Code (Clark County adoption)
publisher: Southern Nevada Building Officials (SNBO) NEC Committee; adopted by Clark County Board of County Commissioners
keyFacts: Amendments were developed by the SNBO NEC Committee; voting limited to Clark County, Henderson, Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, Boulder City, Pahrump, Mesquite, Clark County School District and three industry reps (Preface, p.2)
Clark County Commission adopted on July 15, 2025; amendments and the 2023 NEC effective January 11, 2026 (Adoption by Clark County, p.2)
Adds 110.12(D): conductors/cables may not be abandoned in place in structures regulated by the Building or Swimming Pool Code; must be removed unless the Building Official approves (110.12(D), p.5)
Adds 110.12(F): adjustable settings (GFPE, arc energy reduction, breaker trips, selective coordination, series ratings) must be documented and displayed at the equipment (110.12(F), p.5)
Systems 1000 V and above require third-party/peer plan review, third-party inspection at owner expense, and AHJ-approved testing before permit final (110.30(1)-(3), p.6)
Adds GFCI requirement for receptacles in food/beverage preparation or serving areas regulated by the Health District (210.8(B)(16), p.6)

Dwelling circuits: max 12 outlets on a 15 A luminaire circuit (no general-purpose receptacles) and max 12 outlets on a 20 A 125 V circuit; dishwasher, trash compactor and microwave each need a separate min. 20 A circuit (210.23(F), p.7)

Island/peninsula countertops without a receptacle must get a provision for future receptacle: accessible junction box in the cabinet space with small-appliance branch-circuit conductors (210.52(C)(2), pp.7-8)

Dwelling lighting: wall switch within 6 ft of point of entry, not behind an active door; hallways 10 ft or longer need a switch within 6 ft of each opening; switch for interior light within 6 ft of latching jamb at each keyed exterior entry (210.70(A), pp.8-9)
Multifamily optional calc: deletes 220.84(C)(5) and adds 220.84(D) heating/AC selection list (220.84, p.9)
Existing-load 30-day recording exception in 220.87 not permitted where the feeder/service has PV or wind or any peak load shaving (220.87, p.10)
Customer-owned service conductors may only traverse the property served except through recorded power easements (230.11, p.11)

Service disconnecting means must be at a readily accessible exterior location within 12 ft of the building (otherwise treated as a separate structure), or in a dedicated electrical room with direct exterior access separated by 1-hour construction; not permitted in bathrooms (230.70(A), p.11)

Dedicated electrical room exterior doors need a yellow sign min. 1 sq ft with 1-inch raised/engraved letters ('Electrical Service Disconnect(s) Inside'); a 3-inch yellow floor stripe is required from the door to each disconnect when not the first encountered or multiple (230.70(B), pp.11-12)
Series-rated combinations: all manufacturers and part numbers must be shown on submittal drawings and only those may be installed (240.86, p.13)
Buildings not joined by continuous concrete foundation/footing and roof are separate structures for grounding electrode purposes (250.32(A), p.13)
Concrete-encased electrode (Ufer) required for new buildings/structures with concrete foundations or footings (250.50, p.13)
Plate electrodes deleted from 250.52(A); pipe and plate electrodes are not permitted as grounding electrodes; rod electrodes min. 8 ft and 5/8 in. diameter unless listed (250.52, pp.13-14)
Single rod must be supplemented unless it has 25 ohms or less to earth; multiple rods at least 6 ft apart (250.53(A)(2)-(3), p.15)
All exterior raceways using compression-type fittings must contain a wire-type EGC sized per Table 250.122 (250.120(D), p.16)
Boxes under 8 in. in any dimension: no more than two extension boxes, or one extension box and one plaster ring, unless listed (314.24, p.17)
Ceiling outlet boxes in habitable rooms of dwellings at locations suitable for a paddle fan must be fan-rated or allow direct access to fan-capable framing (314.27(C)(2), p.17)
Exposed PVC conduit must be Schedule 80 (352.10(G), p.18)
EMT: 358.10(B)/(C) deleted; EMT not permitted embedded in concrete/masonry in contact with earth, underground, or in earth fills (358.10, 358.12, p.18)
Appliances supplied by multiple circuits need a permanent warning sign at each disconnect identifying the other circuits (422.30, pp.18-19)
Fuel-dispensing emergency shutoff sign: yellow, 1 sq ft, black 1-inch letters 'Emergency Pump Shutoff' (514.11(D), p.19)
Field-installed neon skeleton tubing less than 8 ft above grade/floor is considered readily accessible and needs guarding (600.41(D), p.19)
Fire pump and emergency feeder concrete encasement for 2-hour protection: minimum 5 in. of concrete (695.6(A)(2)(4), 700.10(D)(2)(5), pp.20-22)

Emergency system fire-protection triggers set at assembly occupancies of 300 or more, high-rises per the AHJ building code, educational over 300, and health care with non-self-preserving occupants (700.10(D)(1), p.21)
Emergency generator sets within 5 ft of a building require a rated separation wall with no openings (700.12(D)(5), p.23)

PV feeder taps with distribution blocks, split bolts, piercing taps etc. must be in a dedicated box/wireway of at least 100 cubic inches labeled 'WARNING PHOTOVOLTAIC POWER SOURCE INTERCONNECTION' (705.12(A)(4), p.24)
Low-voltage cabling in concealed spaces of Type I or Type II buildings must be plenum-rated or in metal raceway (800.24(C), p.25)
notes: Clark County edition (26 pp.) includes the EMT 358.10/358.12 amendment; compare with the Las Vegas/Henderson version dated March 27, 2025. Amendment document states it may be copied without permission (Preface). Text excerpts restate amended NEC sections; the base NEC text is NOT included in this corpus.

title: Southern Nevada Amendments to the 2023 National Electrical Code (version dated March 27, 2025) - City of Las Vegas
publisher: Southern Nevada Building Officials (SNBO) NEC Committee; posted by City of Las Vegas Building & Safety
keyFacts: Cover states 'Version Dated: March 27, 2025' (p.1)
Same SNBO preface and voting membership as the Clark County edition (Preface, p.2)
Contains the same amendment topics as Clark County's edition, including 210.23(F), 230.70, 250.50, 352.10(G) and 358.10/358.12 (Table of Contents, pp.3-4)
EMT not permitted embedded in concrete/masonry in contact with earth, underground, or within earth fills (358.12, p.18)
Exposed PVC must be Schedule 80 (352.10(G), p.17)
notes: Linked from the City of Las Vegas Building Safety Resources page under '2024 CODE ADOPTION' > '2023 NEC'. The document itself has no City adoption statement; the January 5, 2026 effective date comes from the City industry notice (las-vegas-industry-notice-2024-code-adoption). Section-list comparison against the Clark County edition found the same sections (Clark splits 210.70 and 235.405 differently); full word-by-word comparison not performed. City adopting ordinance number for the 2023 NEC not found.

title: Clark County Ordinance No. 5275 - Electrical Code of Clark County (adopts 2023 NEC and Southern Nevada Amendments)
publisher: Clark County Board of County Commissioners
keyFacts: Deletes and re-adopts Title 25, Chapter 25.04 as the 'Electrical Code of Clark County' adopting the 2023 NEC and the Southern Nevada Amendments by reference (Summary; Sections 1-2, p.1)
Conflict rule: Chapter 25.04 governs over the amendments and NEC; the Southern Nevada Amendments govern over the NEC (25.04.010(C), p.2)
Chapter 22.02 (Building Administrative Code of Clark County) governs administration and enforcement of the electrical code (25.04.020, p.2)
Violations are misdemeanors, up to $1,000 fine and/or 6 months jail, each day a separate offense (25.04.030, p.2)
Proposed July 1, 2025, passed July 15, 2025 unanimously (p.3-4)
In force and effect from and after January 11, 2026 (p.4)
notes: Ordinance number partly garbled in the text layer (scan); the file URL names it 005275. A search-engine summary cited 'Ordinance 5257' for the NEC in another table; that conflicts and was not verified - 5275 is what the county codes page links. Page 5 is an e-signature audit trail.

title: Clark County Building & Fire Prevention - Codes (current codes, ordinances, amendments, technical guidelines, FIGs)
publisher: Clark County Department of Building & Fire Prevention
keyFacts: Effective January 11, 2026 the Clark County Building Department adopted the 2024 International codes; permit applications filed from that date (except standard plans) must comply (page intro)
Lists '2023 National Electrical Code' ordinance and '2023 National Electrical Code (NEC) Southern Nevada Amendments' as current (Current Codes / Ordinance; amendments list)
Lists electrical Field Inspection Guidelines FIG-E-001 through FIG-E-014 and TG-90-2025 Electrical Testing Services (Technical guidelines / FIG lists)
notes: The 'Current Codes / Ordinance' list also still shows 2018/2017-era items (e.g. 2017 NEC, 2018 Building Administrative Code); the page does not clearly separate current from prior editions. Several FIG-E documents still cite 2017 NEC section numbers.

title: City of Las Vegas Industry Advisory - Adoption of the 2024 Code
publisher: City of Las Vegas Building & Safety Division
keyFacts: City Council approved ordinances on July 16, 2025 adopting national codes and local amendments including the 2023 National Electrical Code (p.1)
Effective date of the codes is January 5, 2026 (p.1)
Projects with an initial submittal on or after January 5, 2026 must be designed to the 2024 codes (2023 NEC); earlier submittals could use either (p.1)
notes: Ordinance numbers not stated in the notice.

title: City of Las Vegas Building Safety Resources (codes and amendments tab)
publisher: City of Las Vegas Building & Safety
keyFacts: States the City adopted the 2024 IBC, IRC, IEBC, ISPSC, UPC, UMC, IECC, IFC, IWUIC and the 2023 NEC, effective January 2026 (B&S - Codes section)
States the 2019 CLV Administrative Code remains in effect (B&S - Codes section)
Links the 2023 NEC amendments PDF under '2024 CODE ADOPTION' (2024 CODE ADOPTION list)
notes: Page gives only 'January 2026'; the industry notice gives January 5, 2026.

title: City of Las Vegas Administrative Code, 2019 Edition (Ordinance 6769)
publisher: City of Las Vegas
keyFacts: Electrical permit exemptions include cord-and-plug portable appliances, holiday lighting, switch parts, receptacle replacement (not the box), same-rating OCPD replacement, sign electrodes/transformers, theater sets, franchised cable/phone wiring outside buildings, power-limited wiring 50 V or less in single-family dwellings, exposed surface-mounted power-limited wiring, luminaire replacement within Article 314 weight limits, VFD replacement up to 50 HP/100 A not in smoke control, Class 2/3 wiring not part of fire alarm/emergency/smoke control, like-for-like fixed motor/appliance replacement, and utility work (301.4.4, printed pp.25-26)
Contractor must possess or employ a master or qualified individual certification issued or approved by the City of Las Vegas for electrical permits (306.1(2)-(3), printed p.46)

On residential/light-frame job sites with permitted electrical work, a master electrician, electrical qualified individual, or journeyman electrician must be present during work hours in a supervisory capacity (306.1(3)(b), printed p.47)
notes: City website says this 2019 Administrative Code remains in effect with the 2024 code adoption. Exam/card issuance mechanics are not in this document (see ESP entries).

title: Building Administrative Code of Clark County (Clark County Code Ch. 22.02) - 2018 reprint, printed 10-2022
publisher: Clark County Building Department
keyFacts: Reprint states only the Clark County Code is actual law; latest listed amendment Ord. 4917 effective 03-01-22 (cover, p.1)

Electrical permit exemptions: utility installations, listed cord-and-plug portable appliances, like-for-like fixed motor/transformer/appliance replacement, temporary decorative lighting, switch/contactor parts, receptacle replacement (not box), same-capacity OCPD replacement, sign electrodes/transformers, taping splices, removal of wiring, lab experimental wiring, stage sets, certain low-voltage work (incl. replacing light fixtures in single-family dwellings, <=24 V security/doorbell systems), and VFD replacement up to 50 HP/100 A not in smoke control (22.02.200, pp.38-39)
Sheds up to 200 sq ft are exempt from a building permit, but an electrical permit is still required for any electrical work (limited to one lighting and/or one power circuit) (22.02.190(A), p.35)

Contractor must have the appropriate business license and possess or employ a master or qualified individual certification; on residential/light-frame jobs a master electrician, electrical qualified individual or journeyman electrician must be on site during work hours (22.02.250, p.49)
Homeowner permits allowed for an owner-occupied single-family dwelling when exempt under NRS 624.031 and the owner signs the Owner/Builder statement per NRS 278.573 (22.02.265, pp.49-50)

Required electrical inspections: UFER before foundation pour, underground before slab/under-floor cover, rough before framing inspection, other as required, and final before use/occupancy (22.02.475, p.78)
notes: Clark County's codes page still lists this '2018 Building Administrative Code' among current codes; amendments after March 2022 (if any) are not reflected in this reprint - verify against the codified Clark County Code Ch. 22.02.

title: Clark County Field Inspection Guideline FIG-E-012 - NV Energy Requirements
publisher: Clark County Building and Fire Prevention, Field Inspection Division
keyFacts: Services must meet the serving utility's standards in addition to the NEC; listed NV Energy standards are part of the inspection (Interpretation/Field Application, p.1)
Meter working space: 36 in. deep, 78 in. high, 36 in. wide, min. 10 in. from side of service enclosure to obstruction (RPI-2 bullet, p.1)
Minimum 36 in. horizontal clearance from the electric meter panel to the nearest edge of a gas meter (RPI-2 bullet, p.1)
New single-family meter must be on the front of the building facing the serving line or on an adjacent side within 10 ft of the front (RPI-2 bullet, p.1)
Single-meter height 48 in. to 75 in. to center from standing surface (RPI-2 bullet, p.1)
Overhead service mast: RGS or IMC, min. 2 in., max 30 in. unbraced (60 in. if braced), conductors extend min. 18 in. from weatherhead (RR-2 bullet, p.1)
notes: Revised 10/01/2020. Pages 2-4 are figures with no extractable text. Listed on the Clark codes page as 'revised 11/21'.

title: Clark County Field Inspection Guideline FIG-E-007 - Temporary Electrical Power
publisher: Clark County Building Department
keyFacts: Department may allow temporary construction power through the main building service instead of a temp pole (Policy, p.1)
Residential (incl. R-2): panel per Nevada Power Standard Design E-105; meter approved only after footings/foundation complete; at least one GFCI device on the load side (A.1, p.1)
Commercial: meter may be tagged before final for construction/testing; Form #160-1; signs, billboards and cell sites get the meter tag only at building final (B.1, p.1)
notes: Revised 05/08/2024; still cites 2017 NEC Article 590. Page 2 has no extractable text.

title: Clark County Field Inspection Guideline FIG-E-009 - Working Clearance (transformers)
publisher: Clark County Building and Fire Prevention, Field Inspection Division
keyFacts: Clark County does not apply 110.26(A) working clearance to transformers because they must be de-energized for servicing (Field Application 1-4, p.1)
notes: Revised 10/01/2020; cites 2017 NEC 110.26(A).

title: Clark County Field Inspection Guideline FIG-E-004 - Generators
publisher: Clark County Building and Fire Prevention, Field Inspection Division
keyFacts: Generators supplying stationary equipment or connecting to stationary wiring require an electrical permit; portable or vehicle-mounted generators supplying portable equipment per 250.34 do not (Interpretation, p.1)
Grounding electrode system references 250.52 'as modified in the Southern Nevada Amendments' (Field Application, p.1)
notes: Revised 10/01/2020; cites 2017 NEC section numbers - check against 2023 NEC numbering.

title: Nevada Administrative Code Chapter 624 - Contractors (State Contractors Board regulations)
publisher: Nevada Legislature (Legislative Counsel Bureau)
keyFacts: Page header: NAC-624 revised date 4-26; file rev. 6/7/2026 (header)
C-2 Electrical contracting license allows installing any electrical wires, fixtures, appliances, apparatus, raceways and conduits, and residential/commercial wind systems (NAC 624.200(1))

C-2 subclassifications: C-2a electrical wiring; C-2b integrated ceilings; C-2c fire detection; C-2d low voltage systems (fiber optics or not over 91 V); C-2e lines to transmit electricity; C-2f residential wiring (not over 600 V, structures not over three stories); C-2g photovoltaics (not wiring beyond the service panel) (NAC 624.200(2))

Experience documentation: four certificates of work experience, or a current master certification issued by a governmental agency in a substantially similar discipline, or military experience (NAC 624.590(2)(b))
Experience certification waived for endorsement applicants with 4 years licensed in good standing in an endorsing state and no discipline (NAC 624.590(3))
Trade exam waived if the applicant passed an exam offered by an endorsing state approved by the Board, or a NASCLA-accredited exam the Board finds equivalent (NAC 624.600(2))
Three exam attempts; must pass within 6 months of filing; after third failure the application is void and may be refiled after 30 days (NAC 624.600(4))
Board determines which states have substantially equivalent licensing requirements and publishes the list on its website (NAC 624.615(1))
notes: Statutory basis (NRS 624) not downloaded. Nevada does not license individual electricians at the state level in this chapter; individual cards are local (see ESP / Reno entries).

title: NSCB - Licensure by Endorsement and State License Equivalency Chart
publisher: Nevada State Contractors Board
keyFacts: Endorsement waives the Nevada trade exam and experience certification for applicants licensed in states Nevada deems substantially equivalent (Licensure by Endorsement intro)

Requires an active license in the endorsing state, with the same qualified individual, for the past four years, no misconduct investigations/discipline, and a Request for Verification of License from the endorsing state (minimum requirements; How to Apply)
The qualified individual must still pass the Nevada Business and Law examination (minimum requirements)
Arizona chart: Nevada C-2 Electrical maps to Arizona CR-11 Electrical for experience, and to the CR-11 Electrical exam for trade exam waiver (Arizona Equivalency Chart)
Endorsement covers only the trade exam and/or experience requirement; all other documentation still required (Note)
notes: Arizona entry lists only CR-11 for C-2; Arizona residential (R-11) or commercial (C-11) electrical classifications are not listed - unclear whether they qualify. Page last-modified stamp shows 2025-02-11.

title: NSCB - License Requirements (bond, examination, experience, financial)
publisher: Nevada State Contractors Board
keyFacts: Bond amount set by the Board at approval, ranging $1,000 to $500,000 (Bond Requirements)

Qualifying individual must pass the Business and Law (CMS) exam and the trade exam for the classification unless waived; exams by PSI with Nevada sites in Las Vegas, Reno and Elko (Examination Requirements)

Trade qualifier needs at least four full years of experience as a journeyman, supervising employee or contractor in the specific classification within the 15 years before applying (Experience Requirements)
Up to 3 years of experience credit for accredited training/apprenticeship with documentation (Experience Requirements)
A financial statement is required regardless of monetary limit requested (Financial Statement Requirements)
notes: Page stamp 2026-01-09.

title: NSCB - License Examinations
publisher: Nevada State Contractors Board
keyFacts: Applicants pass a business and law (CMS) exam plus a trade exam for the classification; eligibility letter issued after experience is verified (intro; FAQ)
CMS exam is open book (Construction Business and Law Manual for Nevada); trade exams closed book except certain code references (FAQ)
Trade exam may be waived for licensure by endorsement (FAQ)
notes: PSI candidate bulletin for the C-2 trade exam not downloaded.

title: NSCB - Handyman Exemptions (NRS 624.031 summary)
publisher: Nevada State Contractors Board
keyFacts: Repair/maintenance work under $1,000 including labor and materials is exempt from contractor licensing unless conditions apply, e.g. a building permit is required (list item)
Owners building or improving a residential structure for their own occupancy are exempt subject to conditions and an exemption application (list item)
notes: Summary page; NRS 624.031 itself not downloaded.

title: Nevada State Fire Marshal Division Memorandum on permits and inspections (posted by NSCB Nov 10, 2026)
publisher: Nevada Department of Public Safety, State Fire Marshal Division (posted by NSCB)
keyFacts: SFM found contractors starting work without SFM permits and concealing work before SFM inspection (p.1)

SFM will enforce under NAC/NRS 477 and the 2024 International Fire Code: notices of violation (IFC 113.3), stop work orders (IFC 114), administrative citations (NRS 477.240), fines (NAC 477.991) (p.1)
Contractors should confirm whether a project falls under SFM statutory authority before starting, even if the local AHJ has approved it (p.1)
notes: Scanned PDF with no text layer; the .txt is a manual transcription of page 1 only (page 2 not rendered/transcribed). Memo itself is undated on page 1; date taken from NSCB posting (Nov 10, 2026). Relevant mainly to fire alarm / life-safety electrical work in SFM jurisdiction.

title: State of Nevada Public Works Division - Adopted Codes (state-owned buildings)
publisher: State of Nevada Public Works Division
keyFacts: SPWD adopts codes under NAC 341.045, including the 2023 National Electrical Code (p.1)
Code edition is set by the date plans are first submitted; 2018-code designs accepted until June 30, 2025 grace period end (p.1)
notes: Applies to State Public Works projects, not to local jurisdictions. Document revised 2/13/2024. No statewide electrical code for private work was found.

title: NV Energy Electric Service Requirements (ESR) - Southern Nevada, June 2021 Edition
jurisdiction: Southern Nevada (NV Energy / Nevada Power service area)
publisher: NV Energy
keyFacts: Date of publication June 23, 2021; users must confirm the latest revision of each standard online (p.2)
Any deviation from ESR requirements must be approved in writing by an NV Energy representative (Introduction, p.3)

Residential standard service point must be on the street-facing wall or side wall with back of curb to meter edge not over 100 ft and the safe work space in sight from the street (RPI-2 section 4.1, PDF p.282)
Meters only on walls solely owned/controlled by the homeowner; property-line walls not approved (RPI-2 4.4, PDF p.282)
No fences, gates or walls in front of service equipment; power-operated gates do not count as readily accessible; path must be free of landscaping (RPI-2 5.2-5.4, PDF p.282)
notes: Utility-published public PDF (not a government work); copyright field set to government_public only because the schema has no 'public utility' value - review before redistribution. 519 pages, 19.7 MB; text extraction is incomplete for rotated drawings. Could not confirm whether a newer edition than June 2021 exists.

title: Nevada Power Company (NV Energy South) Tariff Rule No. 16 - Service Connections, Meters and Customer's Facilities
jurisdiction: Southern Nevada (NV Energy / Nevada Power service area)
publisher: Nevada Power Company d/b/a NV Energy (PUCN tariff)
keyFacts: For underground service from overhead lines the customer installs, at its expense and per utility standards, the riser conduit to 8 ft above ground on the pole and the underground conductor (A.2.a(1), p.1)
Utility installs a suitable meter at a customer-furnished location that must be accessible for reading, testing and maintenance (A.5, p.3)
In multi-tenant buildings all meters are located at a central point and each is permanently marked (A.5.c, p.4)
notes: PUCN-filed tariff; sheets carry different issue/effective dates (2002, 2008, 2013). Current-version status not verified against PUCN.

title: City of Reno - Electrical / Plumbing Journeyman Cards
publisher: City of Reno
keyFacts: Electrical installations in Reno must be done by a person holding a valid journeyman certificate; apprentices need a card from an approved apprenticeship program (page body)

Exceptions: homeowners; contractors with written supervision agreements on site; holders of reciprocal licenses from another city/county/state, who must obtain the Reno certification after 12 months working in the City (page body)
Electrician exams are ICC G17 Journeyman or G18 Residential; no pre-approval required (Journeyman Electrician section)
ID cards produced by Electrical Safety Professionals (ESP); valid three years; renewable within one year of expiration with reinstatement fee, otherwise re-test (ID Cards section)
Refers to Reno Municipal Code Title 14 for details (page body)
notes: Page cites G17/G18 exams; ESP's June 2026 testing notice lists R-17/R-18 (2023 NEC-based) as the only acceptable new tests - the Reno page may lag.

title: Washoe County - History of Adopted Building Codes (incl. currently adopted codes)
publisher: Washoe County Building Program
keyFacts: Currently adopted: Ordinance 1736, adopted 06/10/2025, effective 07/01/2025, includes the 2023 National Electrical Code ('NEC First Print') with the 2024 Northern Nevada Amendments (Currently Adopted Codes)
Previous: 2018 codes with 2017 NEC effective 01/01/2019 (Ordinance 1625) (history table)
notes: Unincorporated Washoe County only; City of Reno and Sparks adopt separately (Reno effective date not verified from an official source).

title: 2024 Northern Nevada Code Amendments (incl. 2023 NEC) - NNICC, as posted by Lyon County
jurisdiction: Northern Nevada (Reno, Sparks, Washoe, Carson City, etc.)
publisher: Northern Nevada Chapter of the International Code Council (NNICC)
keyFacts: Published by NNICC on February 20, 2025; covers 2024 I-codes, UMC, UPC and 2023 NEC (cover, p.1)
Participating jurisdictions include Carson City, Reno, Sparks, Washoe County, Douglas, Lyon, Storey, Churchill, Elko, Fallon, Fernley and Reno-Sparks Indian Colony (p.2)

Service disconnect may be inside nearest point of entrance or detached within line of sight not over 30 ft; interior allowed with an external remote shunt-trip switch at 7 ft in a 12-in. red triangle (230.70(A)(1), p.57)
Edison-base plug fuses only for replacement; when premises wiring is altered, fuse holders must comply with 240.54 (240.51(B), p.57)
Raceways on roofs must contain a wire EGC (250.120(D), p.58)
EMT not permitted in direct contact with earth or direct burial (358.12, p.58)
Emergency system fire-protection thresholds: assembly 1000 or more persons, buildings above 55 ft, educational over 300 (700.10(D)(1), 700.12(B), p.59)
notes: Hosted by Lyon County, not by Reno/Washoe; NNICC is a chapter of an ICC association (local amendment text, not ICC model code). Status assumes adoption by Washoe County per its Ordinance 1736; each northern jurisdiction's adoption and any local modifications not verified. Edits shown with strike-through in the original may read oddly in the extracted text (e.g. '23 16.8m (75 55ft)').

title: City of Henderson - National Electric Code page (2023 NEC, Southern Nevada Amendments, adopting ordinance)
publisher: City of Henderson Building and Fire Safety
notes: Site returned HTTP 403 (bot protection) to both curl and WebFetch; not downloaded. Amendments PDF link seen in search: https://www.cityofhenderson.com/home/showpublisheddocument/15983/638833433919100000 (also 403).

title: City of North Las Vegas - Codes Adopted By Reference
publisher: City of North Las Vegas City Clerk
notes: HTTP 403 to automated fetch; not downloaded. Search excerpts suggested the page still lists a 2018 Electrical Code (Ordinance 2911) and that North Las Vegas's fire page lists the 2024 IFC effective January 5, 2026; no official confirmation found that North Las Vegas adopted the 2023 NEC or its effective date. title: Electrical Safety Professionals (ESP) - NV Electrician Exam Testing Information notice (June 2026)
jurisdiction: Southern and Northern Nevada (Clark County, Las Vegas, Reno card program)
publisher: Electrical Safety Professionals (nonprofit program administrator)
keyFacts: ESP runs the Nevada Electrical Qualifications Card program; applications are online only (notice header)
New-card exams are bought/scheduled through ICC and taken only in person at Pearson VUE centers since Sept 1, 2025 (notice body)
Acceptable new-card exams are 2023 NEC-based: R-16 Master, R-17 Journeyman, R-18 Residential (notice body)
Cards are 3-year; listed fees $85 for journeyman/residential/low-voltage and $100 for master; late fees rise after 30 days and cards go inactive after 365 days (fee table)
Notice says NV electrical qualification cards are separate from NV State Contractor licenses (notice body)
notes: Not a government site; facts paraphrased, no file stored. Work/apprenticeship hours for new cards are on ESP's site and were not retrieved. The official Clark County / Las Vegas code basis for the card requirement is the admin-code 'master or qualified individual certification' language (see admin code entries).

title: Electrical Safety Professionals (ESP) - Approved CEU Providers and Card Renewal CEU Requirements (updated June 1, 2026)
publisher: Electrical Safety Professionals
keyFacts: Renewal every three years requires 1.8 CEUs (18 hours) for journeyman, residential, sign or low-voltage cards and 3.0 CEUs (30 hours) for master (CEU Requirements)
Must include at least 8 hours of NEC code-change (2023 NEC) and 4 hours of NFPA 70E (2024) from ESP-approved providers (CEU Requirements; renewal summaries)
Classes based on editions older than the 2020 NEC / 2021 NFPA 70E are no longer accepted (intro)
notes: Not a government site; paraphrased, no file stored.
